newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya bond oversubscribed by $52 million.
newsitem.headline: Kenya bond oversubscribed by $52 million.

text.p: The fourth issue of the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) floating-rate treasury bond closed at 7.9 billion shillings ($143 million), 58 percent above the initial offer of five billion shillings, CBK officials said on Wednesday.

"The oversubsription and success of the issue demonstrates a shift from treasury bill investment to the bond which the central bank anticipates in future issues," CBK Director of Banking Reuben Marambii said in a statement.
Jimnah Mbaru, chairman of the Nairobi Stock Exchange, said the success of the issue was a mark of confidence from the public.
"Their performance is remarkable especially because this is an election year," Mbaru told Reuters.
The government bond's popularity has grown tremendously because it offers an attractive alternative to deposits in commercial banks, according to stock exchange floor dealers.
"The existence of a secondary market was a big boon for the bond," said Job Kihumba, chief executive of the NSE.
"It is an easy exit option for investors who might find one year too long to wait for maturity," he added.

The bond is pegged to the 91-day treasury bill and offers a 0.25 percent margin above the quarterly moving average rate of the t-bill. The current quarterly moving average rate for the t-bill stands at 20.108 percent.
The bank said it accepted all applications while secondary trading on the fourth issue will begin on July 7 at the NSE.
The next issue is scheduled for September 29, 1997.
